# What enforces each control

Generated from `hooks/hooks.json`, `skills/agrim-init/templates/config.json.tmpl` and the
`ENFORCEMENT_GATES` registries in `skills/agrim-loop/scripts/{work,state,loop}.py`. Regenerate:

    python3 skills/agrim-doctor/scripts/enforcement_table.py > docs/enforcement.md

**Kinds.** *Python gate*: plain Python in the kit refuses, parks or holds; identical on every
host. *git host*: your repository's own branch protection or CI refuses the merge. *Claude Code
hook*: a `hooks/hooks.json` hook denies the action; Cursor and Codex have no hooks, so it holds
nowhere else. *advice*: the skills ask the agent to do it and no code checks that it did.

**Default (scaffolded)** is the value `/agrim-init` writes from `config.json.tmpl`, read from
that template at generation time. `work.enabled` ships `true` directly as of #2741 (1.0.0)
-- so on a bare `/agrim-init` every `work.py` row below reads `on` unless its own second key
says otherwise. `verify.enforce` ships `false` (#228): the template cannot know a command, and
enforce on with an empty one refuses every `done`. `/agrim-init` turns it on once a verify
command is confirmed (`verify_detect.py confirm`). `/agrim-setup` still writes
`ledger.enabled: true` where it is `null` (unchanged, still off by default).

**Hosts** names where the mechanism holds *by construction* -- a Python gate runs wherever
the kit runs; a hook exists only on Claude Code -- not where it has been run end to end. The
Cursor adapter is not verified in a live session; Codex has partial live validation.

## Controls

| Control | Enforced by | Mechanism | Default (scaffolded) | Hosts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `finish` refused while the PR is open | Python gate | `work.py` `_open_pr_refusal`: refuses `work.py finish` (worktree removal) while the goal's PR is still open, since the state file it would delete is the only record of that PR; fails open when GitHub cannot be read | on — `work.enabled: true` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| `record done` refused while the PR is open, unmerged, unarmed | Python gate | `work.py` `done_refusal`: refuses `loop.py record done` while the goal's PR is open, unmerged and not armed to merge under a policy that would have armed it; under `off` it cannot tell a leave-for-a-human PR from a skipped merge and lets `done` through | off — `work.enabled: true`, `work.auto_merge: "off"` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Dependency hold at pick | Python gate | `loop.py` `_pick_dependency_hold`: leaves a goal unclaimed (no label, no lock, no comment) while a prerequisite it declares is still open, instead of claiming it and parking | on — `discovery.dependency_gate.mode: "on"`; any `mode` other than `off` reads as on, including an absent key or a typo (`_dependency_gate_mode`) | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Dirty root checkout refuses `start` | Python gate | `work.py` `_dirty_root_refusal`: refuses `work.py start` while the root checkout carries tracked, uncommitted edits -- the sign that something edited the base branch directly instead of a worktree | on — `work.enabled: true` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Hard plan gate at PR push | Python gate | `work.py` `_hard_plan_gate_refusal`: refuses to push a branch whose goal has no plan under `.sdlc/plans/`; plain Python, so it is the one plan gate that holds on every host | off — `work.enabled: true`, `gates.hard_plan_gate.enabled: false`; an organisation can lock it on through managed settings | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Merge only when GitHub reports clean AND safe | Python gate | `work.py` `gate`: parks unless GitHub reports the pushed head `mergeable` with `mergeStateStatus CLEAN` (a still-pending required check is armed, not merged) | off — `work.enabled: true`, `work.auto_merge: "off"`; the clean-and-safe verdict is computed and reported even with `work.auto_merge: "off"` -- `gate()` runs before `merge()` returns on off -- only the merge itself is skipped | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Never merge a fork PR or without write rights | Python gate | `work.py` `merge_rights`: never attempts a merge on a fork PR or a repository without write access, and fails closed when rights cannot be determined; the PR stays open and `done` is recorded | on — `work.enabled: true` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Per-run budget: goals per session | Python gate | `loop.py` `_session_count_stop`: stops admitting goals once this session's settled plus in-flight admissions reach the ceiling | on — `budget.max_iterations: 20` (`handoff.after_goals: 20`); `handoff.after_goals` is checked first and wins a tie: at the shipped 20/20 the stop reads HANDOFF, not BUDGET | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Per-run budget: wall-clock and token ceilings | Python gate | `loop.py` `_budget_resource_reason`: stops admitting goals at a phase boundary once the session's minutes, priced Claude-equivalent tokens or measured Codex raw tokens reach a ceiling; each ceiling enforces only when set to a positive number; there is no currency cap | on — `budget.max_minutes: 480` (`budget.max_tokens: 500000`, `budget.max_codex_raw_tokens: 0`); the on/off cell keys off `budget.max_minutes` alone -- the token ceilings still enforce with minutes zeroed, and vice versa | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Plan must be on the goal branch before PR | Python gate | `work.py` `_plan_missing_from_branch`: refuses `work.py pr` while the goal's plan exists on disk but is not committed on the goal branch | on — `work.enabled: true` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Post-PR review gate | Python gate | `work.py` `review_gate`: reads the PR's actual review state, independent of branch protection: `off` checks nothing; `changes` parks on a Request-changes, an unresolved thread or a `sigma:block` comment; `approval` also requires an approval (formal, or a `sigma:approve` comment) | on — `work.enabled: true`, `work.require_review: "changes"` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Research dossier must be on the branch before PR | Python gate | `work.py` `_research_missing_from_branch`: refuses `work.py pr` while the goal's research dossier exists on disk but is not committed on the goal branch | on — `work.enabled: true` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Resume refused: ledger claim held by a live sibling | Python gate | `work.py` `_resume_blocked_by_a_live_sibling`: refuses to resume an existing worktree whose ledger claim belongs to a different, still-live process of the same actor | off — `work.enabled: true`, `ledger.enabled: null` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Resume refused: live foreign agent marker | Python gate | `work.py` `_blocked_by_a_live_foreign_agent`: refuses to resume a worktree whose agent marker names a live process that is not the caller | on — `work.enabled: true` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Review-to-fix cycle cap | Python gate | `work.py` `post_review`: parks the goal once its review-to-fix cycles reach `work.max_review_cycles` (a value below 1 falls back to 3), so a review loop cannot run away | on — `work.enabled: true` (`work.max_review_cycles: 3`) | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Secret-shaped filename refused at commit | Python gate | `work.py` `_secret_refusal`: refuses `work.py commit` when a staged path has a secret-shaped basename (`.env`, `*.pem`, `id_rsa`, `credentials.json`, ...); a basename denylist only, no content scan; `work.allow_secret_paths` lists exact repo-relative exceptions | on — `work.enabled: true` (`work.allow_secret_paths: []`) | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Stale worktree resume refused | Python gate | `work.py` `_stale_resume_refusal`: refuses to resume an existing worktree that is stale against its base, first moving the goal out of the claimed state so the refusal leaves nothing to un-park | on — `work.enabled: true` (`work.rebase_upkeep: "on"`) | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Verify evidence before `record done` | Python gate | `state.py` `done_refusal`: `loop.py record done` exits 4 (REFUSED) without this run's passing verify evidence; the command run is the local goal's `verify_command` frontmatter, else the repo-wide `verify.command` (GitHub-mode goals always use the latter) | off — `verify.enforce: false` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Verify evidence before a merge | Python gate | `work.py` `merge`: refuses the merge (PARK) without this run's passing `loop.py verify` evidence, whether or not `verify.enforce` is set; the command run is the local goal's `verify_command` frontmatter, else the repo-wide `verify.command` (GitHub-mode goals always use the latter) | on — `work.enabled: true` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Branch protection (required checks / reviews) | git host | GitHub refuses the merge; `work.auto_merge: "protected"` merges only where the base requires them | your repository's own settings; Sigma never configures them | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Quality-drift eval corpus | git host | `evals/run.py` fails the CI job; blocks a merge only where branch protection requires the check | Sigma's own public CI on push/PR; nothing installs it into your repository | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Decision registry invariants | Claude Code hook | `hooks/decision_gate.py`: denies an edit (PreToolUse) that assigns a registered invariant a violating value; fails open on its own errors | on once `/agrim-decide` writes `.sdlc/decisions.json` in an adopted repo -- `.sdlc/config.json` present (#2737), so a repo holding only `decisions.json` is not gated; `gates.decision_gate.enabled: false` turns it off. On every host, `decision_gate.py check .` is a manual backstop -- nothing in `work.py` or `loop.py` runs it, so there it is not a gate | Claude Code only |
| Hard plan gate at edit | Claude Code hook | `hooks/plan_gate.sh`: denies the edit itself (PreToolUse), in an adopted repo (#2737), when no plan under `.sdlc/plans/` is fresher than `plan_freshness_hours`; honours `touch .sdlc/.allow-direct-edits` only while the key is not org-locked ON -- under `.sdlc/managed-settings.json` the sentinel is ignored (#2138); an accelerator for the PR-push gate above, which holds on every host | off — `gates.hard_plan_gate.enabled: false` | Claude Code only |
| New issue needs a priority label | Claude Code hook | `hooks/issue_field_gate.py`: denies a `gh issue create` (PreToolUse on Bash) that carries no `priority:P<n>` label, so an issue is born ranked | always on (no key) inside an adopted repo -- `.sdlc/config.json` at or above the project dir (#2737); inert elsewhere; fails open | Claude Code only |
| Stop gate | Claude Code hook | `hooks/completion_gate.sh`: refuses to let the session stop (Stop), in an adopted repo (#2737), with source changed in the working tree and no fresh plan under `.sdlc/plans/`; honours `touch .sdlc/.allow-direct-edits` | off — `gates.stop_gate.enabled: false` | Claude Code only |
| Independent review | advice | The skills ask the agent to dispatch it. An independent reviewer subagent is dispatched with an author-blind brief; the core binds the verdict to one PR, head and brief generation, and cannot prove the maker did not influence the reviewer. | on — `review.independent: true` | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Irreversible actions park | advice | the loop's instructions ask the agent to park rather than run a deploy/delete/overwrite/spend/migrate | `gates.irreversible_actions: ["deploy", "delete", "overwrite", "spend", "migrate"]`, `gates.on_block: "park"`; no code reads these keys | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Plan review before implementation | advice | `agrim-plan-review` asks the agent to review the plan before any edit; `loop.py emit gate --gate plan_review` only records a verdict, no code reads it | always on (no key) | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| SDLC policy reminder on every prompt | advice | `hooks/agrim_gate.sh`: injects the standing policy that asks the agent to follow the 7-phase spine on every prompt; enforces nothing | on wherever `.sdlc/` exists (or `SIGMA_GATE_GLOBAL=1`). Not this hook: Codex and Cursor get the same standing rule only as an opt-in rule file, `/agrim-init --codex` (managed block in `AGENTS.md`) or `/agrim-init --cursor` (always-applied `.cursor/rules/sdlc.mdc`) | Claude Code only |
| SessionStart policy brief | advice | `hooks/session_start.sh`: injects the SDLC policy brief and a doctor-lite install self-check at session start, which asks the agent to follow the conventions; warns, never blocks | off — `session_start.enabled: false`; the brief needs `session_start.enabled`; separately, the ledger-watcher staleness warning fires whenever `ledger.enabled` is `true`, with no key of its own | Claude Code only |
| Strategy alignment (FIX-FIRST) | advice | `agrim-plan-review` asks the reviewer to send back a plan that contradicts the north-star; no code checks it | always on (no key) | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |
| Test-first implementation | advice | `agrim-implement` asks the agent to write the failing test first; no code compares test and source order | always on (no key) | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex |

## Every hook in hooks/hooks.json

| Event | Matcher | Hook | Blocks? | Control |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UserPromptSubmit | — | `agrim_gate.sh` | no | SDLC policy reminder on every prompt |
| UserPromptSubmit | — | `time_track.py prompt` | no | — (time tracking) |
| PostToolUse | WebSearch\|WebFetch | `research_capture.py` | no | — (knowledge capture) |
| PreToolUse | Bash | `issue_field_gate.py` | yes | New issue needs a priority label |
| PreToolUse | Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit\|NotebookEdit | `plan_gate.sh` | yes | Hard plan gate at edit |
| PreToolUse | Edit\|Write\|MultiEdit\|NotebookEdit | `decision_gate.py` | yes | Decision registry invariants |
| PreToolUse | Skill | `time_track.py skill` | no | — (time tracking) |
| Stop | — | `completion_gate.sh` | yes | Stop gate |
| Stop | — | `time_track.py stop` | no | — (time tracking) |
| SessionStart | — | `session_start.sh` | no | SessionStart policy brief |

## Not yet in this table

Pick-time gates in `feature_owner.py`, `feature_propagate.py`, `promote.py` and `feature_labels.py` (`gate_at_pick` and the promote-time label checks) are not registered yet: they back the README's "Human approval gate, in one transition" and "Findings become work" rows, and a follow-up registers them. `work.py` also refuses to load a config with `ledger.receipt_sharing: true` (not supported yet); that is a config refusal, not a control on the work, and is deferred with them.

Reported, not enforced: live status (`action_log.enabled`, off) and agent liveness (`agent_watch.enabled`, off) show state and refuse nothing, so they are monitors, not controls. There is no rollback control at all: `work.py` aborts a failed rebase, and nothing reverts a landed goal. Acceptance criteria are the verify rows' command source, above. Cursor / Codex parity is the Hosts column, not a row.
